finding.claim: Unauthenticated SSRF: POST /hooks/test sends a server-side POST to an attacker-supplied URL with no validation.

trace.note: POST /hooks/test registered on the `pub` router, which has no auth middleware in this file
req.body.callback passed unmodified as the axios.post URL
r.status returned to caller, giving a status oracle for internal hosts and ports

finding.guards_checked: None on the path: no auth middleware on pub, no scheme allowlist, no host/IP allowlist, no DNS pinning, no redirect control (axios follows redirects by default). Mount point of `pub` in the app is not in the repo and could not be verified.

verdict.guard_found: none. routes.js:19-22 has no validation, no allowlist, and no middleware on pub. requireAdmin (routes.js:7-12) is attached only to admin via admin.use at routes.js:12, not to pub.
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate: routes.js:20 passes req.body.callback unmodified to axios.post, and routes.js:21 returns r.status to the caller. Within this file, the pub route has no auth or URL validation, so an unauthenticated caller controls the URL. The one caveat is that the mount point of pub is outside the repo; if the app mounts it behind an auth middleware, the attack needs an authenticated user, so the severity depends on that unverified mount.

finding.claim: Admin-gated SSRF: GET /diagnostics/fetch sends a server-side GET to an admin-supplied URL with no validation.

trace.note: requireAdmin applied to every route on the admin router
Only r.status returned, a status-code oracle for internal probing

finding.guards_checked: Role check only (routes.js:8, :12). No scheme, host, resolved-IP, or redirect validation. session middleware that populates req.session is not in the repo and could not be verified.

verdict.guard_found: Role check at routes.js:8 (requireAdmin, returns 403 unless req.session.role === "admin") applied to the whole admin router at routes.js:12. No hostname, IP, scheme, or redirect validation exists on the sink at routes.js:15.
verdict.reason: Every trace line checks out (routes.js:7-8, 12, 14-16), but the source req.query.url at routes.js:15 is only reachable through the admin-only router gated at routes.js:8 and :12, so it is not controllable by the unauthenticated or low-privilege attacker this finding requires. The remaining issue is an admin-supplied URL, which is a much weaker, admin-trust case rather than a remote SSRF. Caveat: the session middleware that sets req.session is not in the repo, so the strength of the admin gate itself is unverified.
